newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Tianjin Zhongxin offers 100 mln shares at US$0.68.
newsitem.headline: Tianjin Zhongxin offers 100 mln shares at US$0.68.

text.p: Tianjin Zhongxin Pharmaceutical Group Corp Ltd launched an initial public offering comprising 100 million new shares of one renminbi each at US$0.68 per share on Thursday.
A company statement said 20 million shares would be available for public for subscription and 80 million would be privately placed out.
The issue price of US$0.68 per share represents a historical price earning ratio of 8.8 times based on net earnings per share of Tianjun Zhongxin for year ended December 31, 1996.
Historical net earnings per share of the group for 1996 are US7.7 cents.
The company, which is seeking primary listing on the main board of the Stock Exchange of Singapore, expects to raise net proceeds of US$63 million from the initial public offering.
The money will be used to finance new factories, repay bank borrowings and for working capital.
Turnover for the group was 211.25 million renminbi in 1996 against 198.32 million the previous year. Profit after tax for 1996 was 146.30 million renminbi against 94.85 million previously.
The IPo, led managed by DBS Bank, closes on June 25 and will start trading on June 27.
Tianjin Zhongxin is an established name in traditional Chinese medicine in China. Its main product includes Suxiao Jiuxinwan, one of the 15 emergency Chinese medicine used in China.
The group's product are mainly marketed under Great Wall, Cyprus Time and Health brandnames widely recognised in China.
It also has joint ventures with foreign companies such as SmithKline Beechem Corp and Bieffe Medital S.P.A.
